topic: cross-thread topic identity and incremental continuity in work communication

open_gaps.description: Which evidence combinations actually establish or refute continuity of a concrete work matter across independent workplace messages, conversations, attachments, email, and Teams remains open. The corpus supports adjacent-domain signals but does not validate subject, customer/project names, conversation ancestry, referenced artifacts, commitments, or state compatibility as target-domain identity evidence.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: ("work item identity" OR "work matter identity" OR "business event coreference") AND (email OR "workplace communication" OR enterprise) AND (cross-thread OR cross-document OR cross-source)

open_gaps.description: The application-specific decision policy remains open: the relative cost of false merges versus false splits, thresholds for attachment versus rejection, and exact semantics/calibration of CONTINUE, NEW, and UNCERTAIN must be determined from msgloom requirements and empirical evaluation. The reviewed literature does not establish that false merges should receive a higher explicit cost.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve through application requirements and empirical decision-policy evaluation: define the operational consequences and costs of false merges and false splits, specify CONTINUE/NEW/UNCERTAIN semantics, build a representative labeled validation set, sweep decision thresholds, measure precision/recall and cost-weighted error, and calibrate thresholds against the chosen product risk policy.

open_gaps.description: The msgloom correction and identity-state model remains open. Stable Topic IDs independent of generated labels or source thread IDs, versioned identity assessments, supersession links, immutable evidence lineage, and general MERGE/SPLIT correction are project-level engineering choices not established by this corpus. They require design-document review, implementation prototypes, invariants, and correction-focused tests.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve through architecture and implementation work: define stable Topic-ID and identity-version schemas, evidence-lineage and supersession models, MERGE/SPLIT correction operations, referential and history-preservation invariants, then validate them with prototypes, migration scenarios, correction replay tests, concurrency tests, and persistence benchmarks.

open_gaps.description: There is no direct production-domain evidence in this corpus for longitudinal work-matter identity across Outlook email and Microsoft Teams. News, Wikipedia, image-recognition, public-health linkage, knowledge-graph, and database-process results cannot establish production accuracy or representativeness for msgloom.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: (enterprise OR workplace) AND (email OR "Microsoft Teams" OR chat) AND (cross-thread OR longitudinal OR cross-conversation) AND (topic identity OR task tracking OR case tracking OR event coreference)

open_gaps.description: How partial, subevent, evolving, or otherwise non-transitive relations should map onto work-matter continuity is unresolved. CDEC-WN shows that event relations can be non-transitive, but no reviewed paper defines the corresponding semantics for workplace Topics.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: ("partial event identity" OR "subevent relation" OR "event evolution" OR "non-transitive coreference") AND (workflow OR task OR case OR workplace)

open_gaps.description: The best operational strategy for Phase 2 evidence seeking is unresolved. Retrieval-based event-coreference search is promising adjacent-domain evidence, but msgloom still needs engineering benchmarks for bounded historical retrieval, candidate generation, latency, and whether additional context changes identity decisions.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with controlled benchmarks over representative msgloom data: compare candidate-generation and historical-retrieval strategies at fixed recall targets, vary retrieval windows and top-k bounds, measure latency and memory cost, record how often retrieved context changes the identity decision, and select an operating point that meets both accuracy and latency requirements.

open_gaps.description: Calibration under non-stationary workplace streams remains unresolved. Selective-classification guarantees assume calibration data representative of deployment, while cross-corpus coreference results show material distribution sensitivity.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: ("selective classification" OR abstention OR "confidence calibration") AND ("distribution shift" OR nonstationary OR streaming OR "concept drift") AND (text OR coreference OR clustering)

open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 2. open_gaps.description: The best operational strategy for Phase 2 evidence seeking remains unresolved. Retrieval-based event-coreference search and global-context models show that additional evidence can matter, but msgloom still needs engineering benchmarks for bounded historical retrieval, candidate generation, latency, retrieval stopping rules, and whether retrieved context actually changes identity decisions correctly.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with application-specific retrieval benchmarks. Implement competing candidate-generation and historical-retrieval strategies; vary time windows, candidate limits, lexical/semantic filters, conversation ancestry, artifact links, and stopping criteria; record retrieval recall, end-to-end latency, token/context cost, decision changes, correction rate, and false-merge/false-split effects. Compare no-retrieval, bounded retrieval, and progressively expanded retrieval on the same labeled stream. doi-10-18653-v1-2022-emnlp-main-58 and doi-10-18653-v1-2023-emnlp-main-294 motivate evidence seeking but do not determine msgloom's operational bounds.

open_gaps.description: Calibration under non-stationary workplace streams remains unresolved. open_gaps.suggested_search_query: ("selective classification" OR abstention OR "confidence calibration" OR "selective prediction") AND ("distribution shift" OR nonstationary OR streaming OR "concept drift") AND (text OR NLP OR coreference OR clustering)
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after round 2. Paper 1705.08500 supports selective-risk or abstention mechanisms, while 2011.12249 and 2104.05022 provide evidence of cross-corpus distribution sensitivity, but the reviewed corpus does not establish a reliable calibration or abstention procedure for continuously changing workplace communication streams.
